text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: route=/generate p95 latency > 400ms for 5m. Metric note: kv_cache.evictions/sec jumped from ~0.8 to 22 across inference-cache-az-a. Paging SRE Pager.

Maria G: Ack. I'm pulling up the cache dashboards and traces. Appears correlated with a runtime TTL change that started around 09:05 UTC.

Josh L: On call, joining now. Any deploys in last 30m?

Kevin R: I promoted a TTL tweak in a canary at ~09:04 UTC to reduce memory use. Was gated but looks like it reached ~30% of traffic. I didn't expect that to increase eviction rate this much.

ops-bot: @Kevin R flagged as potential deploy source.

Amy S: Short-term mitigation: throttle the canary (stop serving canary traffic) and increase cache pool target size by +2 nodes. Also, disable the aggressive eviction policy in the runtime for 10m.

Maria G: Executing ops now. Commands:
```bash
# reduce canary percentage to 0
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  https://deploy.redwood.internal/canary -d '{"service":"runtime","percent":0}'
# bump desired cache capacity
kubectl -n infra scale statefulset inference-cache --replicas=5
```

incident-bot: Canary reduction accepted. Cache scale started (pods pending).

Josh L: Good. I'm toggling runtime arg --eviction-aggressiveness=normal -> in prod config.

Kevin R: Rolling that back too. Also effective to mute any paging rules that are catching noisy eviction spikes so only the composite will page.

SRE Pager: Handing to Josh L for the incident until 16:30 UTC.

Josh L: Taking lead. Initial numbers: p95 for /generate peaked ~420ms, error rate unchanged. Hit rate for kv_cache fell to 72% during spike.

Maria G: Running a quick group-by of eviction tags to see if specific prefixes are dominating:
```sql
SELECT prefix, sum(evictions) AS ev_count
FROM cache_evictions
WHERE cluster = 'inference-cache-az-a' AND ts > now() - interval '20 minutes'
GROUP BY prefix
ORDER BY ev_count DESC
LIMIT 15;
```

Maria G: Output: top prefixes are spread across multiple model-shard prefixes, not single hot key. Suggests increased churn rather than single hot-key abuse.

Amy S: For alert hygiene: propose we adjust noisy rule eviction-host-surge that currently pages on evictions/sec > 5 for 1m. Change to a paired rule that pages only when (evictions/sec > 10 for 4m) AND (kv_cache.hit_rate < 0.80 for 4m). That should cut down repeated wakeups.

Josh L: I will create that composite alert now and mute the old one for the incident window.

Josh L: Actions executed: muted eviction-host-surge (mute until 1867016800), created composite alert kv-cache-failure-composite with expr: (avg_over_time(kv_cache.evictions_per_sec[5m]) > 10 and avg_over_time(kv_cache.hit_rate[5m]) < 0.80) for 4m. Pages SRE Pager + posts to #incidents.

incident-bot: Composite alert created and active.

Maria G: Cache pods came up, eviction/sec trending down to ~1.5, hit rate recovering to ~88%. p95 dropped to ~230ms.

Kevin R: I'll add low-overhead admission logging in the canary runtime (not full traces) to gather per-prefix admission and eviction events. PR incoming after incident.

Amy S: Support outreach: I'm pinging Support to proactively message any customers with high-volume generation usage. No customer error reports yet, but some customers might have seen higher latencies.

SRE Pager: Please document customer-impact assessment in the incident ticket: increased p95/p99 latency for a subset of generation traffic; no user-facing errors; mitigations applied.

Josh L: Handoff plan: I'll keep watch for 30m then hand to Maria for follow-up. If composite alert fires, page SRE Pager immediately.

Maria G: Confirmed stabilization: evictions down, hit rate steady at ~90%, p95 stable around 210ms. Closing live mitigation actions. Moving to post-incident follow-up.

Amy S: Post-incident monitoring changes I'd like:
- New dashboard panels: eviction/sec per shard (heatmap), hit_rate 1m/5m/15m comparisons, evictions normalized by active keys.
- Alert tuning: make host-level evictions P3, cluster-level composite P1, and an automated runbook link in every page message.

Josh L: I'll update the alert configs and add the runbook link (runbook: https://runbooks.redwood/internal/kv-cache-evictions).

Kevin R: Follow-ups I own: revert TTL defaults doc, add admission counters, and add a small canary smoke test that simulates eviction churn before promoting TTL changes. Target: PR + tests by EOD.

Maria G: Adding follow-up items to the incident ticket INC-2026-0147:
1) Alert rewrite: implement composite rules and demote noisy pages (owner: Josh L).
2) Observability: add heatmap and normalized eviction graphs (owner: Amy S).
3) Runtime: admission tracing and pre-promote churn test (owner: Kevin R).
4) Autoscaler policy review: increase buffer to avoid immediate scaling during short churn spikes (owner: Maria G).

Amy S: Scheduling 30m post-incident sync tomorrow 11:00 UTC to walk through dashboards and thresholds.

Maria G: Posting quick summary: root cause - TTL canary promotion increased churn, leading to higher evictions and lower hit rate -> increased p95 on /generate. Mitigations - throttle canary, scale cache, revert eviction aggressiveness, create composite alert, add dashboards. Follow-ups assigned.

incident-bot: Incident transitioned to post-incident state. Ticket INC-2026-0147 created.

SRE Pager: Resolved oncall handoff. If trend returns, reopen or page.

Maria G: Closing thread. Please add :thumbsup: if actions/owners look correct.

Josh L: :thumbsup:

Amy S: :thumbsup:

Kevin R: :thumbsup:

Maria G: Thanks team. :sparkles:
